issues.description: revoke_error exposed via API without explicit auth-level gating despite author flagging it as a security concern
issues.detail: The PR author asks in the description whether displaying revoke_error is safe. The answer is: error strings from arbitrary backends routinely leak paths, network endpoints, credentials fragments, and stack-ish details. Shipping this on the public lookup endpoint without a sudo/root-only gate or a sanitization pass is wrong shape. Either redact, or require elevated capability to see it.

issues.description: Renaming FetchLeaseTimes to FetchLeaseInfo breaks the public exported API for no functional gain
issues.detail: FetchLeaseTimes is an exported method on ExpirationManager. Out-of-tree consumers and downstream forks call it. The rename is cosmetic — the old name still describes what callers want. Keep FetchLeaseTimes as a thin wrapper or just leave the name alone. Don't churn exported symbols to make the godoc read nicer.

issues.description: metrics label still says fetch-lease-times after the rename, inconsistency baked into telemetry
issues.detail: metrics.MeasureSince uses the literal "fetch-lease-times" key. If the function is now FetchLeaseInfo, either keep the metric name (and acknowledge it in a comment so the next maintainer doesn't 'fix' it) or rename it as a deliberate breaking telemetry change. Silent mismatch between code and metric is exactly the thing that confuses ops six months from now.

issues.description: Test mixes nil context and t.Context() in the same call, sloppy and inconsistent with surrounding tests
issues.detail: namespace.RootContext(t.Context()) was substituted for namespace.RootContext(nil) in one spot while two other touched tests kept nil. Pick one. Drive-by context changes that don't match the rest of the file are the kind of unrelated churn a maintainer has to mentally filter out of a diff.

issues.description: OpenAPI schema marks path as Required but namespace_path and revoke_error are not — verify the response contract matches
issues.detail: path is declared Required: true in the framework path spec, which is fine for normal leases but worth confirming for edge cases (irrevocable leases loaded from disk where Path might be empty). If Path can legitimately be empty, Required is a lie and clients generated from the schema will break. Quick check, not an architecture problem.

issues.description: Test coverage for the new fields is one line checking path; namespace_path and revoke_error are not exercised
issues.detail: TestSystemBackend_leases gets one assertion on path. namespace_path and revoke_error — the two fields that actually carry security-relevant content — have zero test coverage. Add a test that registers a lease in a child namespace and asserts namespace_path, and one that forces a revoke failure and asserts revoke_error shape. Otherwise the schema fields are aspirational.

review.summary: Small patch, mostly does one thing, diff is readable. The actual functional change — surfacing path, namespace_path, and revoke_error on lease lookup — is fine in shape. Two real problems: the author themselves flagged revoke_error as potentially sensitive and shipped it anyway on a non-privileged endpoint, and the FetchLeaseTimes rename is gratuitous churn on an exported API with a now-stale metrics label. Tests cover one of three new fields. NEEDS-WORK: gate or sanitize revoke_error, revert or alias the rename, fix the metric, add tests for the other two fields.
